label: early-middle original-phase input of t/k/o/2/g/y, when the sequence began with i/f/s/1/h/0/m/u
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase: 99.9% of activation mass. It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The input token matters most: t, k, o, 2, g and y carry about 94% of the mass (lift 3-6x), and w, q, 3, l, e and r almost never fire it. Most mass falls at positions 2-6, peaking at t=3-4, and about 92% is on the first occurrence of a token. The input token alone gives precision of only about 9%. Firing is gated by history: rates are much higher when the first original token is i, f, s or 1 (lift 3-4x, and the top examples nearly all start with f/i/1/s), and weaker when it is h, 0, m or u. This first-token gate is an imperfect stand-in for a distributed hidden-state dependence. Seen-sets and second-token variants did not get past F1 of about 0.45, so precision and recall both stay incomplete. Magnitude is largest for t, k, o and 2 at t=3-5 in sequences starting with f/i.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: t, k, o; t=2: k, t, 2, o; t=3: k, t, o, 2) and the first original token (most: i, f, s, 1, h, m; least: 2, e, t, y); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, L=8 & t=10, L=9 & t=11.
